business_scope.primary_industry_name: Bulk Vessel Brokerage of Agricultural Soybeans and Yellow Corn

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Bilateral Investment Treaty between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China (signed 12 November 1986, as amended)
Double Taxation Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the People's Republic of China (signed 27 January 1990, as amended by the Protocol of 25 September 2013)
Convention Establishing the European Free Trade Association (Stockholm Convention, 1960; Switzerland founding member)
Agreement between the European Community and its Member States, of the one part, and the Swiss Confederation, of the other, on the Free Movement of Persons (1999)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (Geldwaeschereigesetz, GwG; SR 955.0) of 10 October 1997, as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (Strafgesetzbuch, StGB; SR 311.0) arts. 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR; SR 220) arts. 697j-697m (register of beneficial owners, in force since 1 July 2015); Swiss Federal Act on the Commercial Register (SR 220.110); Ordinance on the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV; SR 221.411); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national identity card of every natural-person beneficial owner holding, directly or indirectly, at least 25% of shares or voting rights of the Aktiengesellschaft
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or national identity authority of the holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Switzerland has been party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 1973; consular legalization is not required for documents originating in apostille-competent jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and up-to-date commercial registry extract for any corporate shareholder or beneficial owner above the UBO threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-apostille jurisdictions, Swiss consular legalization at the competent Swiss embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing (or equivalent) for each corporate shareholder and corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registry or competent government agency of the corporate entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization at the competent Swiss embassy or consulate in the issuing country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and material trading counterparties against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, (ii) the OFAC SDN and OFAC country-specific lists, (iii) the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, (iv) the Swiss SECO consolidated sanctions list, and (v) international and domestic PEP databases; the notary must document the screening results before authenticating the deed of incorporation, and the opening financial intermediary must independently complete PEP and sanctions verification under GwG arts. 3 and 4 and AMLO-FINMA before account activation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index of Switzerland (www.zefix.ch); official filings and name scrutiny are handled by the cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the registered seat, applying the HRegV structural rules.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (Firma) of an Aktiengesellschaft must contain the term 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' (Art. 950 CO). The free part of the name must be in a Swiss official language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or, if in a foreign language, only to the extent that it is customary in Swiss trade usage. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and clearly distinguishable from all names already registered in Switzerland (Art. 951 CO; HRegV art. 34). Latin script is standard; any non-Latin-script denomination must be accompanied by a Latin-script transliteration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banca (requires FINMA banking license and specific privilege notice)
Insurance / Assurance / Versicherung (requires FINMA insurance license)
Swiss / Schweizer / Confederation / Federal / Eidgenossenschaft (reserved for state and public-law entities or requires special ministerial authorization)
Fiduciary / Fiduciaire / Trust (regulated activity terms requiring authorization or mandatory disclaimers)
Stock exchange, clearing house, or other terms implying a government monopoly or public-law status
Any token implying a business activity for which the company is not licensed or authorized
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name decision issued by the cantonal Handelsregisteramt, the applicant may file a written objection (Einsprache) with the same office within 30 days of service of the decision. If the objection is dismissed, an administrative appeal may be lodged within 30 days before the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (commercial register inspectorate), and further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht). Alternatively, the applicant may submit a fresh name application with a modified distinctive element without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not admissible as the sole registered seat. The Aktiengesellschaft must designate a physical seat in a Swiss municipality where its administration operates or where its statutory books, minutes, and records are accessible (Art. 51 CO). A commercial domiciliation provider may supply a physical address, mail forwarding, and statutory records management, which is accepted Swiss practice; a purely virtual address without a physical Swiss presence or serviceable capacity will be rejected by the commercial register and by opening financial intermediaries.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk: for an unlicensed wholesale commodities brokerage company, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection is below 5%. Unannounced visits occur mainly in connection with suspected money-laundering reports (GwG), tax or VAT audits, or targeted commercial register supervisory reviews; no routine physical inspection program applies to this industry classification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance inquiry (Firmenabklaerung) at the cantonal Handelsregisteramt
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal fee schedule; typically CHF 50-100 per name inquiry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Statuten) for the Aktiengesellschaft
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed cantonal notary at the registered seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff based on statutory capital and drafting scope; market benchmark CHF 1,500-2,500

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce operator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official gazette tariff under the Federal Act on the Commercial Register; CHF 250-400 per insertion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation entry fee in the Commercial Register (cantonal and federal components)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office and the Federal Commercial Register Office (Federal Office of Justice)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: HRegV and cantonal tariffs; AG incorporation entry CHF 600-1,200 plus federal surcharge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment and first filing of the beneficial owner register under Art. 697j CO, including PEP, UN, OFAC, EU, and SECO sanctions screening dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed notary and corporate services provider engaged by the company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for Stage 1 UBO piercing and screening setup; CHF 700-1,200 excluding external database subscriptions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille authentication and certified translation of identity and corporate existence documentation bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal apostille office of document origin and licensed translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fees and prevailing market translation rates; CHF 300-700 for multi-document packages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss legal counsel fees for pre-incorporation structuring, UBO piercing, name clearance, and Stage 1 contract and AML framework review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Stage 1 corporate and AML mandates; CHF 4,500-8,000 or negotiated fixed fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-account-opening AML/CFT compliance pack for the relationship bank (UBO declarations, source-of-wealth statements, payment rail confirmation for LC and SWIFT wire)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank KYC fee schedules and notarial certification costs; CHF 800-1,500

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Switzerland: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620–643 (formation, capital, registration of the Aktiengesellschaft), Articles 626 and 629 (mandatory contents of the deed and articles of association), Article 633 (paid-up capital confirmation), Article 727a (audit exemption), and Articles 640–643 (commercial register entry and attainment of legal personality).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug) acting under the supervisory authority of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Schweizerisches Handelsregisteramt) at the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP); electronic filing conducted through the notary via the eGRIS system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Anmeldung zur Eintragung ins Handelsregister – certified application for entry into the Commercial Register, together with the notarized deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde), the articles of association (Statuten), and the paid-up capital confirmation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Nominal share capital of at least CHF 100,000 (Art. 621 OR); a minimum of CHF 50,000 must be paid up in cash into a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) with a licensed Swiss bank. The bank must issue an unconditional paid-up capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) before the commercial register application can be filed; the funds remain blocked and become freely available to the company only upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: 1) The subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000 divided into registered shares of CHF 1,000 each is hereby confirmed; the minimum paid-up tranche of CHF 50,000 has been deposited in a blocked escrow account with a licensed Swiss bank, and the Executive Board is authorized to obtain and submit the paid-up capital confirmation to the Commercial Register. 2) The registered office is established in Zug, Canton Zug, Switzerland; the deed of incorporation and articles of association are adopted as presented, and the Executive Board is directed to file all formation documents and procure registration. 3) The following officers are appointed: President, Secretary, and Statutory Auditor; signatory powers are fixed per the corporate records, and the Executive Board is authorized to open bank accounts, register for VAT, and complete all ancillary governance filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation name clearance and corporate governance design
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Federal Department of Justice); Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug for name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the Zefix database to confirm the proposed corporate name, including the required legal form suffix Aktiengesellschaft or its abbreviation AG. Verify absence of identical or confusingly similar names, secure an appropriate CHF domain name, and prepare the draft articles of association reflecting the dual board and shareholder structure, capital split, and possible audit exemption. Formally reserve the name with the Handelsregisteramt Zug if desired.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application
Proposed articles of association (draft Statuten)
Identity documents of incorporators
Declaration of intended registered seat in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected on grounds of ambiguity or conflict, file a revised name reservation with a distinctive element; where the registry issues an official refusal, appeal in writing to the Cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority within 10 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary’s Office of Canton Zug (Öffentliches Notariat des Kantons Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators appear before a Zug notary to execute the deed of incorporation and adopt the articles of association. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the capital breakdown, and any declaration to opt out of the ordinary audit in accordance with Article 727a OR. The deed shall contain the company name, registered office, share capital, par value, type of shares, board composition, signatory rights, and permitted business purpose of bulk grain and agricultural commodity brokerage. The notary then certifies the deed and prepares the registration packet.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport or ID of each incorporator and director
Capital table detailing subscribed and paid-up shares
Written declaration of audit exemption, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises defects, promptly amend the draft Statuten and re-execute the deed; any ambiguity concerning business purpose is cured by a clarifying notarial annex prior to forwarding to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked escrow account and deposit of minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank in Canton Zug (e.g. Zuger Kantonalbank or comparable bank licensed by FINMA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation blocked account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss bank, deposit at least CHF 50,000 of the nominal capital, and instruct the bank that funds are disposable only after successful registration in the Commercial Register. Provide the bank with the notarized deed extract, identification of the board, and beneficial owner declaration. After verification, the bank issues the paid-up capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung) explicitly addressed to the Handelsregisteramt Zug.
required_dossiers: Notarized extract of the deed of incorporation
KYC/client onboarding forms
Beneficial ownership declaration
Authorization to open the escrow account pending registration
Confirmation of the corporate purpose and source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requeries ownership or source-of-funds documentation, submit an enhanced corporate background statement; if the bank declines the account, open an alternate FINMA-licensed bank account and re-issue the deposit instruction without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Audit exemption assessment and corporate appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; notified within the corporate records; no registrable filing required for the exemption itself
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board assesses whether the company qualifies for the audit exemption under Article 727a OR, requiring fewer than ten full-time equivalent employees, a balance sheet total under CHF 2 million, and turnover under CHF 2.5 million for two consecutive fiscal years. If qualified, the general meeting or founders declare the waiver; this waiver is recorded in the deed or in the first shareholders’ resolution. The board also formally appoints the President among its members and designates the secretary for minutes and filings.
required_dossiers: Founders’ declaration of audit waiver
Signed officer acceptance letters
List of board members with nationality and residence details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statutory presumptions do not apply, the company must mandatorily appoint an external audit firm licensed by the Federal Audit Oversight Authority (FAOA) before registration; the audit mandate must be attached to the commercial register file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation application with the Cantonal Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug (Cantonal Commercial Register Office of Zug)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the certified application for entry into the Commercial Register, including the notarized deed, articles of association, paid-up capital confirmation, board resolutions, and officer consents. The application must state the directors’ names, nationality, and authorized signatory categories, and must confirm that the capital has been validly subscribed and paid. The Commercial Register reviews legal compliance with the OR and checks the name and seat. Upon approval, the company is registered and granted legal personality ex tunc.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Certified articles of association (Statuten)
Bank paid-up capital confirmation (Liberierungsbestätigung)
Signed application form for commercial register entry
Specimen signatures of each authorized signatory
Officer consent declarations and identity copies
Declaration on audit exemption and auditor appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for clarification or a query (Vorbescheid), respond with corrective documentation through the notary within 21 days; if the application is refused, file an administrative appeal with the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority within 10 days and, if necessary, correct the statements and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce and extraction of official records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon final registration, the Commercial Register instructs publication of the incorporation notice in the SHAB. The publication confirms the company name, seat, share capital, board members, and signatory rights. The company then obtains an official current extract (Handelsregisterauszug) confirming legal personality and authority to commence operations. No separate application is required for the SHAB publication.
required_dossiers: None – publication is triggered by the Commercial Register
Request for official extract of the registered entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If published data contains any discrepancy, request a rectification entry via the Handelsregisteramt Zug; where publication is delayed, request expedited handling citing the statutory publication deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-formation federal registrations (VAT, social insurance, and customs trade registers)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (FTA/ESTV); Swiss Compensation Office (AHV); Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG); Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) if physical grain imports commence
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the commercial register extract, register the company with the FTA for VAT if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000; register as an employer with the AHV compensation office and mandatory accident insurance (Suva) once personnel are hired. Because the entity trades agricultural commodities in bulk, register with FOAG for applicable grain import tariff-rate quota administration and with FSVO if the company physically imports or places feed grains on the market. If the company remains a pure commission-based brokerage without physical handling, FSVO registration is not triggered.
required_dossiers: Official Commercial Register extract
VAT registration form (FTA)
AHV employer registration form
Insurance policy declarations with Suva
Customs/import declarations if physical grain import is commenced
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FTA or AHV rejects the application for missing data, correct the fields online and re-submit within 30 days; assessments for late VAT registration may be appealed to the Federal Tax Administration with a written corrective statement; any customs quota issue is cured by amending the import declaration with FOAG.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial license is mandated for commission-based bulk grain and soybean brokerage under ISIC 4631. Where the company transitions to physical import or storage, the relevant authority becomes the Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG) for agricultural trade quotas and the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO) for feedstuffs regulation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for the current pure-brokerage scope. Optional registrations: agricultural import quota registration with FOAG and feed business operator registration with FSVO should physical grain handling, storage, or importation be added.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) in coordination with the Cantonal Environmental Protection Office of Zug
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no fixed industrial installation; administrative brokerage activity is not listed in Annex I of the Ordinance on the Environmental Impact Assessment (UVPV/EIAO), and no full EIA or EIA registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to brokerage operations; no industrial wastewater, VOC, or waste streams are generated. If future storage is added, compliance with the Federal Waters Protection Act (Gewässerschutzgesetz), the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control (LRV), and the Ordinance on Movements of Waste (VeVA) would apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Standard office workplace clearance under the Swiss Labour Act (ArG) and accident prevention rules of Suva; fire safety certification must be issued by the Cantonal Building Insurance of Zug (Gebäudeversicherung Zug) following an inspection of the registered office; structural load clearance applies only to physical grain storage installations, which are not present in the current brokerage scope.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions, AFC); online portal: www.estv.admin.ch and dedicated VAT e-portal (Suche / VAT access) at estv.admin.ch for filing and registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss Aktiengesellschaft is automatically assigned a Swiss Business Identification Number (UID/IDE) upon Commercial Register incorporation at the cantonal register. VAT registration is a separate mandatory step with the Federal Tax Administration: the AG (or a foreign non-established entity) must file Form 'Registrierung für die Mehrwertsteuer / Anmeldung zur Mehrwertsteuerpflicht' (VAT registration notification) through the FTA e-portal. Non-resident entities supplying goods or services in Switzerland must register once their annual worldwide turnover from Swiss-taxable supplies reaches CHF 100,000, and must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative unless they have a Swiss branch or permanent establishment. The FTA issues a 9-digit UID followed by MWST/IVA number; registration becomes effective ex nunc and requires bookkeeping evidence of turnover thresholds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not permit US-style check-the-box elections. Available statutory elections and regimes: (i) VAT group registration election (Mehrwertsteuergruppe) under Art. 12 of the Swiss VAT Act for closely affiliated companies; (ii) small-business exemption under Art. 11 VAT Act for turnover below CHF 100,000 with right to opt into standard taxation; (iii) Group Taxation (profitable group taxation) for corporate income tax from fiscal year 2020 at cantonal/federal level; (iv) participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains under Art. 69-70 of the Federal Act on Direct Taxation; (v) hybrid mismatch neutralisation under Swiss domestic rules implementing BEPS Action 2 — no elective carve-out is available for mismatching structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Swiss Federal Value Added Tax - Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover from taxable supplies with a Swiss place of supply; a de facto zero threshold applies to non-resident suppliers of electronically supplied services and certain B2B services subject to reverse charge; simplified registration applies for foreign businesses making only occasional deliveries in Switzerland.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based transactional clearance mandate. E-invoicing and QR-bills are voluntary alternatives to paper invoices. VAT returns (formular 1010) must be filed electronically through the FTA e-portal on a quarterly or annual basis depending on taxpayer volume, with SIX/Multipay integration for payment. Swiss customs clearances via the e-dec / ZEBIS system serve as the operational export-control interface.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported by the supplier or on its behalf out of Swiss customs territory, evidenced by the customs export declaration (Ausfuhrdokument). For an AG acting as bulk vessel broker for soybeans and yellow corn (ISIC 4631), zero-rating of brokerage commission services applies when the recipient is a foreign-resident business and the services relate directly to goods in transit or to international transport of the goods, or when the services are economically used abroad; goods stored in Swiss free ports remain outside the Swiss VAT territory and are exempt under bonded-warehouse rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / ZEBIS electronic record with customs clearance stamp or electronic transit reference T1)
Bill of Lading (shipped-on-board negotiable maritime bill for bulk grain/corn cargo) or CMR/CIM contract of carriage for overland transport

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence of foreign currency receipt for the underlying commodity sale) and the cash-sale/contract confirmation showing title transfer and foreign destination
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-checked by the FTA against customs exit records, commercial contracts, shipping manifests, and banks' inward remittance files. Erroneous or fraudulent zero-rating triggers immediate reassessment at 8.1% VAT plus default interest at 4% per annum and administrative fines up to four times the evaded tax under Art. 182 VAT Act; structured sham export schemes are prosecuted as tax fraud under Art. 186 VAT Act and Art. 146 Swiss Criminal Code, with custodial penalties possible and personal director liability; clawback is unlimited for fraud and gross negligence and subject to a ten-year limitation only for ordinary negligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB / Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse, Börsenstrasse 15, Zurich); complemented by the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for external financial policy. The SNB is the sole monetary authority, retains the right to intervene in the free-floating franc market, and operates the cross-border payments statistical surveillance system; it does not issue foreign-exchange operating licences.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland grants full current-account and capital-account convertibility under IMF Article VIII; no central-bank permit, exchange licence, or currency-cover requirement applies to trade or capital remittances. The CHF floats freely; the exchange-rate floor of 15 January 2015 was permanently removed. Profit repatriation is legally unrestricted, but a Swiss AG paying dividends to its foreign shareholder faces the 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) unless a double-taxation treaty exemption or refund path applies. Banks additionally enforce AMLA origin-of-funds duties, so first deposits can be delayed while the economic background of the contributing shareholder is verified. Practical limitation: the SNB requires Swiss banks to report any counterparty transaction flow equal to or exceeding CHF 10 million in a calendar month for balance-of-payments statistics; the corporate must provide sufficient purpose and trade data for that filing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender rules exist in Switzerland. Export proceeds from bulk grain, soybeans, and corn sales (USD, EUR, BRL, or other currencies) may be retained indefinitely in domestic Swiss bank accounts, in any currency, with no mandatory conversion into CHF and no statutory repatriation deadline. The sole statutory duty is the bank's own reporting to the SNB under the Ordinance on Cross-Border Payment Statistics for payments reaching CHF 10 million per counterparty per month; the exporting AG must merely supply accurate payment reference and counterparty details to enable the bank to comply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (CHF/EUR/USD) with dedicated Capital Escrow sub-account for equity injection
Operational multi-currency corporate account with commodities trade-finance and LC division
Capital Escrow Account (Kapitalkonto) and domestic operational CHF account
Operational secondary-account for CHF liquidity buffer

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low for the principal treasury and LC-backed trade settlement; marginal as a collection-only sub-rail. A Swiss AG must keep core treasury funds with a FINMA-authorised bank or a licensed payment institution under the FinIA and AMLA; offshore digital EMIs (UK, Lithuanian, Caribbean, or other non-FINMA licences) cannot issue letters of credit in the name of the Swiss AG, cannot act as prime treasury counterparties, and are automatically graded high-risk by Swiss banks. A Swiss-licensed fintech holding a payment-institution licence (for example a FINMA-authorised Zug-based payment institution) may be used for small-value collections and pre-screening of inbound FX receipts, but all grain settlement and working-capital flows must run over SWIFT and LC rails through an SRO-member bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permitted for a low-risk Swiss AG under the FINMA video-identification framework (AMLO-FINMA Art. 12/13), provided the UBO and directors are identified through a FINMA-certified digital identity provider. In practice, however, Tier-1 banks require physical appearance for treasury facilities above CHF 1.0 million or for the first letter-of-credit request: the UBO or the CFO must attend an in-person KYC and business-origin interview at the bank's Zurich, Geneva, Lugano, or Zug branch. A Swiss resident authorised signatory with an active SIX identity may reduce but not fully waive the physical-meeting mandate for higher-risk jurisdictions or offshore ownership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO structure: bearer shares or offshore intermediate holdings conceal the ultimate natural-person shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified share-register extract confirming no outstanding bearer share certificates (CO Art. 622); signed UBO declaration under AMLA Art. 4; full group chart ending at natural persons; Zefix company extract; identity and address proof of the natural-person UBO; if an offshore holding is used, a substance letter, audited accounts, and a source-of-funds statement from that holding entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Equity injection funded by an unrelated lender or an unexplained third-party advance rather than the shareholder's own resources.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements of the subscribing shareholder; executed sale and purchase contracts between the AG and commodity suppliers; pro-forma invoices for soybean and yellow corn cargoes; intercompany loan agreement with arm's-length interest; board resolution authorising the borrowing; audited annual financial statements (OR 958) where available; declaration that no unlicensed lender or virtual-asset transfer was used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice pricing deviates from prevailing CBOT or platts benchmarks, signalling under-invoicing or over-invoicing between related grain traders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBOT settlement prices for the pricing date; broker ticket or clearing statement; charter party with freight split; SGS, Intertek, or Control Union weight and quality certificates; detailed sales ledger showing FOB or CIF price basis and tender period; any back-to-back sale contract demonstrating the gross trading margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions nexus in the physical grain chain: Russian, Belarusian, or Ukrainian counterparties, OFAC SDN flags, or untracked bulk carriers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening reports from SECO, OFAC SDN, and EU consolidated lists run at contract, shipment, and settlement dates; vessel name and IMO number with AIS tracking record; charterer UBO declaration; phytosanitary and fumigation certificates proving lawful origin; contractual covenant that the cargo is not of sanctioned origin and will not transit an embargoed port.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment anomaly: funds directed to an entity not named on the invoice or to a non-bank financial institution outside the hard-currency cluster.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed addendum to the supply contract expressly designating the payment beneficiary; bank reference and SWIFT/BIC information matching global LEI or FATCA records; original bill of lading; written confirmation from buyer and seller stating the commercial rationale; if a transferable LC is used, the UCP600 transfer/advice order and the confirming bank's written consent.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital is transferred by SWIFT MT103 or MT199 from the parent's or subscriber's own bank account to the Swiss AG's account at UBS Switzerland AG (SWIFT: UBSWCHZH80A), ZKB (SWIFT: ZKBKCHZZ80A), or the Zuger Kantonalbank escrow; the instruction must state the purpose as 'Kapitalerhöhung' (capital increase) or 'Zeichnungsschein' subscription and the bank requires a notarised board minute, the share-register update, and confirmation that the remitter is the exact subscriber. Intercompany loans are routed by MT103 with reference 'Intercompany-Darlehen' together with the executed loan facility, an arm's-length interest schedule, and an AMLA Art. 4 origin-of-funds statement. This AG will issue equity injection documentation in either CHF, USD, or EUR; no SNB exchange-control permit is required. Any aggregate counterparty flow above CHF 10 million per calendar month is automatically disclosed to the SNB by the bank under the Cross-Border Payments Statistics Ordinance. Future dividend payments to the foreign parent will attract the 35% federal withholding tax unless the applicable double-taxation treaty grants exemption or a refund application is filed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement rails used for bulk soybean and corn purchases: (a) SWIFT MT103 or MT103 STP for direct supplier remittances in USD, EUR, or CHF; (b) irrevocable, transferable letter of credit issued by MT700 and advised or confirmed by a second international bank for the account of the Swiss AG in favour of the exporter, governed by UCP600; (c) MT101 batch or MT202 COV for nostro-covered multicurrency disbursements. Domestic networks: SIC or SIX Interbank Clearing for CHF; SEPA/TARGET2 for EUR; Fedwire/CHIPS via correspondent banks for USD. Every disbursement must be supported by the commercial invoice, bill of lading or FBL, port or warehouse receipt, SGS/Intertek quality and weight certificate, phytosanitary certificate, and the CBOT-derived price lock note. Payment to a beneficiary not named on the commercial invoice is prohibited unless the beneficiary is the assignee expressly entered into the transferable LC under UCP600 rules; all records are retained by the bank for the SNB statistical-review file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC foreign-exchange forward (outright) versus USD, EUR, and BRL under ISDA 2002 with a credit-support annex, executed with UBS, ZKB, or a FINMA-licensed bank treasury desk.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for restricted or illiquid settlement currencies relevant to grain trade (UAH, ARS, and an onshore-linked CNH NDF), used solely to hedge receivables or payables in those currency zones.
Cross-currency swap (CIRS) matching USD-denominated letter-of-credit payables to the Swiss AG's EUR or CHF revenue streams for tenors of up to 12 months.
Purchased vanilla foreign-exchange options and zero-premium collar structures to cap USD/CHF or EUR/CHF movement without selling uncovered optionality.

CBOT-listed corn (ZC) and soybean (ZS) futures transacted through a licensed commodity brokerage as a directly linked hedge of the physical cargo; the hedge is documented as a commercial risk-reduction transaction under Swiss Code of Obligations Art. 211.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (Jahresrechnung) together with the statutory audit report (Revisionsbericht) deposited in the Commercial Register as a public record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register of the seat canton (e.g., Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Department of Justice and Police through the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deposit within 12 months of the balance sheet date; for the standard 31 December balance sheet date, filing is due by 31 December of the following year, following approval at the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The commercial register may compel deposit with coercive administrative fines up to CHF 5,000 (Art. 943 CO); knowingly false filings expose the board of directors to criminal liability (Art. 325 Swiss Criminal Code); persistent default triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off of the company under Art. 731b CO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (Generalversammlung) package comprising the notice, agenda, approved annual financial statements, dividend resolution, discharge of the board and signed minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None; corporate record retained in the statutory minute book (Protokollbuch) at the registered office and made available to shareholders and the statutory auditor upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be convened within 6 months after the close of the business year (no later than 30 June for a 31 December year-end) in accordance with Art. 699 para. 2 CO; minutes signed without undue delay thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or late holding of the AGM constitutes a breach of the directors' statutory duties; the competent court may order compliance on shareholder or creditor petition, and commercial register authorities may impose execution deadlines with coercive fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal, cantonal and municipal corporate income tax return (Steuererklärung) attaching audited financial statements, tax computations and the audit report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the seat canton (e.g., Amt für Steuern des Kantons Zug) acting as collecting agent for the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year taxpayers must file by 31 March of the succeeding year; extensions to 30 September, and in exceptional cases to 31 December, are available upon reasoned request in most cantons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest plus procedural fines up to CHF 5,000; assessed-at-estimate uplifts of up to one-third of the tax where books are deficient; deliberate concealment triggers tax-evasion proceedings under Swiss direct-tax criminal law

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer) periodic return and annual VAT settlement covering brokerage commissions on bulk grain, soybean and corn transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration — VAT Division (ESTV/AFC, Hauptabteilung Mehrwertsteuer, Berne)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly returns are due within 60 days after each quarter-end (31 May, 31 August, 30 November and 28 February); semi-annual and annual filing is limited to taxpayers below the CHF 250,000 annual-turnover threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing and late-payment interest; administrative fines up to CHF 8,000 for negligent failure and up to three times the evaded tax for wilful default under the Swiss VAT Act; serial non-filing may trigger registration suspension and enforcement measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer social insurance settlement and declaration covering AHV/IV/EO/ALV (old-age, disability, loss-of-earnings and unemployment) contributions and salaried-employee statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) acting on behalf of the Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV/OFAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly social security contributions must be remitted by the 10th of the following month; the annual employer settlement and declaration is due by 31 March following the payroll year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest at 5% per annum plus default surcharges of 5% to 15% of unpaid contributions; directors and legal representatives are personally liable for withheld employee portions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Share register (Aktienbuch) verification and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) confirmation certified at the AGM record date, recording the identity and beneficial ownership of every holder of registered shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: None; statutory record maintained at the registered office (or with a disclosed third-party custodian) and open to shareholder inspection; no annual UBO filing is made to the Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The register must be updated without delay upon each transfer notification and in practice within 10 business days; full register verification and UBO declaration confirmation is completed at each AGM record date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or incomplete Aktienbuch entries give rise to board criminal liability for false business certificates; the company may suspend voting and related shareholder rights until the beneficial-owner declaration is supplied (Art. 697k para. 4 CO); commercial register fines may be imposed for evident deficiencies

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory ordinary audit (ordentliche Revision) applies where a company exceeds any two of three thresholds for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets above CHF 20 million, sales turnover above CHF 40 million, or an annual average of 250 full-time employees; ordinary audit is unconditionally required for stock-exchange-listed companies and issuers of bonds; below these thresholds a limited audit (Kurzrevision) applies, and the AGM may dispense with audit entirely only if the company does not exceed 10 full-time-equivalent employees and is not otherwise subject to ordinary audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss statutory accounting standards codified in Arts. 958–963b of the Code of Obligations (Swiss GAAP in the Code of Obligations); IFRS is permitted for individual annual accounts and mandatory for listed issuers under SIX Exchange Regulation; Swiss GAAP FER is the accepted voluntary standard for consolidated and group reporting

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland maintains no annual UBO filing obligation with the Commercial Register; instead, the Aktienbuch constitutes the statutory ownership record and must be updated without delay after each transfer once the shareholder supplies the written beneficial-owner declaration. The board of directors must re-verify the register at each AGM and before any dividend payment; shareholders refusing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner have their voting, dividend and related membership rights suspended in accordance with Art. 697k para. 4 CO until the declaration is made

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,200–8,000 per year in the Zurich/Zug market for registered office, correspondence and statutory agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–14,000 for a limited audit (Kurzrevision); USD 25,000–55,000 for an ordinary audit (ordentliche Revision) of an internationally active agri-commodity trading stock company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None at the federal level. The Swiss federal statutory corporate income tax rate is effectively 8.5% on profit after tax (approximately 7.83% pre-tax), subject to cantonal and communal taxes which are levied in addition. The aggregate headline rate in Zug, where the entity is presumed to be registered for its Web3 and commodity brokerage profile, currently approximates 11.9% to 12.5% depending on the applicable communal factor; a conservative blended statutory headline rate of 18% reflects the maximum combined rate for Swiss corporations with commercial pass-through activities in certain cantons. No general statutory tax holiday exists for bulk agricultural commodity brokerage. Availability of holding company or mixed company status has been abolished under the 2020 corporate tax reform (STAF); however, the patent box and R&D super-deduction may apply only to qualifying IP and research activities, not to bulk grain trading.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal and cantonal corporate tax return (Formulaire de taxation / Steuererklärung für juristische Personen) filed via the e-filing portal of the tax administration (Swiss Federal Tax Administration ESTV and the Cantonal Tax Administration of Zug, e.g., 'eSteuer' or the dedicated cantonal software). The federal return incorporates the S1 form (principal tax declaration) and S2 supplementary boxes for corporate entities
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 6 months after the end of the fiscal year, but in extended practice the tax return filing deadline is set by the cantonal authority; Zug typically allows filing until 30 June of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers. The statutory deadline for submission to the federal and cantonal authorities is generally 6 months from the fiscal year-end; guest or non-resident-controlled companies may face earlier filing instructions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered seat, UID (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer), tax period, balance sheet date, legal form code for AG, and the name of the responsible audit firm.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG held by non-residents, the company's UID and commercial register extract must identify the beneficial owner. The declaration must be signed by the board of directors; virtual or power-of-attorney signatures are not accepted unless previously authorized by the cantonal tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before taxes as per the statutory standalone financial statements prepared under Swiss Code of Obligations (OR Art. 958).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident parent companies cannot file a consolidated return in Switzerland; the Swiss AG must file separate standalone accounts. Only the Swiss entity's statutory profit is subject to Swiss corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt capital gains (profit from disposal of tax-privileged participations if the 10% participation threshold and 12-month holding period are met).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only if the Swiss AG holds at least 10% of the share capital of a foreign company; gains from active trading in bulk grain commodities are ordinary income and must be reported in Box 1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions, including business expenses, depreciation, and provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses directly tied to Swiss source income or justified by the commercial purpose are deductible. Payments to non-resident affiliates require arm's length documentation; hidden profit distributions will be reclassified by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for hidden profit distributions and hidden equity contributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any transaction price deviating from arm's length in transactions with non-resident related parties must be self-declared here. Failure to disclose may lead to penalty assessments and interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying dividend income from a 10%+ qualifying shareholding or a shareholding with a market value above CHF 1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The reduced participation exemption applies only if the subsidiary is subject to an effective corporate tax rate of at least 15% in its residence state; a tax ruling from the cantonal authority should be obtained for foreign dividend flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: S2, Box 2 - Local / Master File TP schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of controlled transactions with foreign related parties and the applied transfer pricing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG must complete the TP schedule if the aggregate controlled transaction volume exceeds the Swiss Ordinance on Transfer Pricing thresholds (typically CHF 250,000 for related-party services and goods).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of Swiss anticipatory tax (35% on distributions of dividends, interest, and royalties) withheld or recoverable under the DTA network.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident shareholders, the Swiss AG must report all distributions and submit declarations for refund procedures on foreign withholding taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: S2, Box 4 - Net wealth tax / capital tax declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal capital tax base (equity less qualified participations and domestic intercompany receivables).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even for a non-resident owned AG, the Swiss capital tax applies at cantonal/communal level based on the company's Swiss equity, no minimum exemption for non-residents.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission is punishable by a procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 2,000 against the responsible officer, plus a formal 'Nichtablieferungsbusse' of 0.1% of the assessed tax for each month the return remains outstanding, capped at 10% of the tax due. In case of failure to submit after formal reminder, tax may be assessed by estimation under reservation of later revision; interest on arrears at 4.5% per annum accrues. Deliberate evasion attracts a fine up to 250% of the tax evaded, and in severe cases, criminal conviction for tax fraud under Article 186 of the Swiss Federal Tax Act (StHG).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% (Swiss anticipatory tax, Verrechnungssteuer) on gross cash dividends and economically equivalent distributions, including constructive dividends and hidden profit distributions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident corporate shareholder resident in a treaty jurisdiction may reclaim the excess Swiss anticipatory tax over the treaty rate by submitting the Swiss Form 82 (Rückerstattungsgesuch / demande de remboursement) to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) DTA division. The shareholder must provide a certificate of residence / tax residence certificate (TRC) from the competent foreign tax authority, generally within the calendar year following the dividend payment or within the specific treaty deadline (typically three years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was distributed). Practically, the Swiss paying agent withholds the statutory 35%, and the investor obtains a partial refund as follows: (i) obtain TRC and Form 82; (ii) file with ESTV; (iii) ESTV refunds the difference (35% minus treaty rate). In low-risk treaty situations (e.g., EU/OECD partners), the refund may take 3-12 months. A Swiss AG cannot 'pay net of treaty rate' unless a specific advance ruling (Säulenerlass) or a notification procedure has been accepted by ESTV; in practice, full withholding at 35% is expected.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory interest and royalty withholding tax (anticipatory tax) is 35% on Swiss-source interest from debentures/bonds issued or guaranteed by the Swiss company and on movable capital income; ordinary bank interest from independent Swiss banks is exempt. Statutory royalties from licensing IP to a Swiss resident are generally exempt if they constitute income from exploitation of patent or software rights; but certain lease of moveable property may attract 35% on rental income. Treaty rates for a Swiss AG engaged in bulk agricultural commodity brokerage will be: interest 10% under the OECD Model treaty, and in practice 0% under many Swiss DTAs where the beneficial owner is the recipient and the interest is paid to a treaty-resident. Dividend DTA rates: 0% for qualifying holdings (10% or more) under most Swiss tax treaties, 15% generally for portfolio dividends. Royalties DTA rates typically 5% to 10% for IP royalties; however, because the entity's ISIC 4631 activity is agricultural wholesale, IP royalties are not expected in the ordinary course.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: In CHF: Local File is required if the aggregate value of controlled transactions with related parties exceeds CHF 250,000 for goods or services, or CHF 100,000 for interest, per tax year. Master File threshold: if the multinational group's total consolidated turnover exceeds CHF 900 million, a Swiss Master File statement and country-by-country reporting notification are mandatory.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - preferred for commodity trading of soybeans and corn; if possible using exchange-quoted prices or comparable independent broker quotes.
Resale Price Method - applicable for low-risk distribution functions performed by the Swiss AG.
Cost Plus Method - suitable for agency and brokerage service functions with limited risk.
TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method) - most common for determining arm's length net margins for routine commodity brokerage and logistics coordination.
Profit Split Method - applicable for highly integrated transactions or where both parties make unique and valuable contributions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply the EU's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as a domestic doctrine, but the Federal Act on the Implementation of International Tax Transparency Standards and the revised Circular 4 (ESTV, Steuervertretung) impose substance requirements under the tax avoidance provisions. A Swiss AG must maintain: actual office premises in Switzerland, qualified directors or employees performing substantive management activities, board meetings in Switzerland, and full accounting records. A 'letterbox company' or shell structure with only nominee directors will be disregarded under the spiritual theory of management (statutarischer Sitz), and profits may be reattributed to the place of effective management. The OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) minimum standards also require the brokerage function to be supported by real personnel who conclude and negotiate contracts, manage logistics contracts, and bear commodity price risk if claiming entitlement to trading profit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Swiss Federal Tax Act, Art. 186)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false or incomplete documentation such as fabricating transportation costs, under-reporting brokerage commissions on bulk soybean or corn trades, using fictitious supplier invoices to reduce gross profit, or concealing Swiss bank accounts and profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A fine of up to 250% of the tax evaded; if the evasion is committed by intentional use of forged documents, false records, or a criminal conspiracy, imprisonment up to three years for responsible directors and tax advisors. Penalty interest at 4.5% per annum is mandatory, and a criminal conviction is entered in the Swiss criminal record.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly and severally liable for restitution of evaded taxes if they signed the unlawful tax return or participated in the scheme. Additionally, the Federal Administrative Criminal Law Act (VStrR) permits seizure of the director's Swiss assets and a travel ban or exit prohibition (Ausreisesperre) while the criminal tax investigation is pending. In severe cases, extradition procedures under the mutual legal assistance treaty may be triggered; a director resident in Switzerland may face preventive detention pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the Swiss AG in Zug solely to receive high-margin commodity brokerage commissions while all negotiation, decision-making, risk-taking, and logistics functions are performed by the foreign parent or by offshore employees with no Swiss presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment by ESTV under the place of effective management doctrine; all attributed profit is taxed as hidden profit distribution at 35% anticipatory tax plus cantonal/federal direct taxes. Capital tax may be reassessed at a deemed minimum equity of 10% of assets, and the company's commercial register entry may be struck off with forced liquidation if the corporate form is abused.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to ensure a minimum physical, personnel, and operational presence can be personally liable under Swiss company law (Art. 754 OR) for damage to the tax authority and creditors. Directors may be required to repay any distributions made while the company was insolvent; a personal criminal fine is possible under Art. 86 para. 2 of the Criminal Code for failure to maintain proper books and records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing fraudulent refund claims for the 35% Swiss anticipatory tax withheld on dividends or interest paid to non-residents, e.g., by submitting false TRCs from jurisdictions with treaty rates lower than 0%, or arranging back-to-back loans through conduit entities to artificially access lower withholding rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: According to Art. 14 of the Anticipatory Tax Act (VStG), claim taxes are subject to a penalty equal to the unlawfully refunded amount, an additional fine of up to 100% of the claim, and an interest surcharge of 5%. Criminal penalties for subsidy fraud under Art. 14 VStrR extend to imprisonment up to five years, and banks or intermediaries involved lose their safe-harbor protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The board members must sign personal declarations that the facts stated in Form 82 are true; deliberate fraud causes direct liability of the signatory with no corporate indemnification under Swiss law. The ESTV may publish the conviction and impose a banking freeze on personal accounts held in Switzerland.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving trade settlement proceeds from bulk agricultural commodity trades without performing customer due diligence; accepting payment from an unknown vessel broker, using a third-party intermediary in a non-treaty state, or deliberately structuring SWIFT wire transfers in tranches below CHF 15,000 to defeat transaction reporting obligations; conducting trades through shell counterparties in high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Art. 10 of the Swiss AML Act of up to CHF 500,000 for negligent money laundering; aggravated money laundering under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code carries imprisonment of up to five years. FINMA licensing infractions for unregistered financial intermediaries may lead to a fine of up to CHF 1 million and a prohibition from operating in Switzerland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable under the Swiss Corporate Criminal Liability Act if the offense arises from the lack of adequate organization (Art. 6 VStrR). Personal imprisonment up to one year is possible for directors who knowingly approve trades where the grain collateral documents are fraudulent; a travel ban is commonly imposed while money laundering investigations proceed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain and submit TP Local File / Master File for related party grain brokerage and logistics transactions exceeding CHF 250,000; or implementing an arbitrary 2% net margin protocol that deviates from the tested arm's length margin selected by the Swiss tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Procedural fine up to CHF 10,000 plus a record-keeping penalty of 0.1% of the inappropriate transaction volume per month of delay; the tax authority may estimate the arm's length price based on its own benchmark and issue a hidden profit distribution assessment, resulting in additional corporate income tax of up to 18% plus 35% anticipatory tax on the deemed distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the Swiss Tax Ordinance, the duty to produce books and records rests on the management; directors can be fined up to CHF 10,000 personally for refusing to produce documentation, and if the resulting assessment causes insolvency, directors may be held liable for negligent loss of corporate assets under Art. 754 OR.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting to withhold and remit the statutory 35% anticipatory tax on actual dividends declared by the Swiss AG to its non-resident shareholder, or paying excessive management fees, interest, or broker commissions to a related party abroad without arm's length justification, thereby converting a taxable distribution into a deductible expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate penalty equal to the unpaid anticipatory tax; estate tax claim remains enforceable against the company. Directors are guilty of an offense under Art. 24 VStG and are individually subject to a fine equal to the unpaid tax if the company is insolvent. Criminal fines up to CHF 30,000 plus costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability without limitation for the unpaid anticipatory tax due to human error or willful disregard; the board's own assets can be attached in execution proceedings initiated by ESTV. Directors have a duty to notify the general meeting to withhold; failure to do so is a serious breach of fiduciary duty.
